notes.1745: Title Implementation of AI to Robot Dynamics; printed Lecture Number 55 and footer 1.
notes.1746: Contents roadmap: dynamics revision, FFNN, forward dynamics pipeline, MLP inverse dynamics on 2R, and DeLaN inverse dynamics on 2R. Footer 2.
notes.1747: The introduction lists nonlinear friction, backlash, cable flexibility, compliance and contact among difficult effects. Learning targets include forward/inverse dynamics and residuals. Adaptation requires data and an update mechanism; it is not automatic. Printed footer 3 inspected separately.
notes.1748: Full equation M(Θ)Θddot+C(Θ,Θdot)+G(Θ)=τ. C is the Coriolis/centrifugal generalized-force vector in this notation, not an unmultiplied n×n matrix. All position/velocity/acceleration/M/C/G/τ definitions inspected. Inverse map takes positions, velocities and accelerations to torque; feedforward/computed torque/tracking applications. No explicit friction/contact term in the displayed nominal equation. Footer 4.
notes.1749: Forward dynamics input (Θ,Θdot,τ), output acceleration, Θddot=M inverse(τ−C−G). Applications simulation, RL, MPC, digital twins. Motion requires integration after instantaneous acceleration; invertibility/model scope declared. Footer 5.
notes.1750: All approximation, data-driven and differentiability bullets were inspected, together with the box naming Deep Lagrangian, Hamiltonian and physics-informed networks. Representation capacity and derivative availability do not establish trained accuracy. Printed footer 6 inspected separately.
notes.1751: Forward 2R diagram: six inputs θ1 θ2 θdot1 θdot2 τ1 τ2, two illustrative 32-neuron hidden layers, ReLU/tanh labels, two acceleration outputs. Arm diagram θ1 relative horizontal, θ2 relative first-link extension, lengths l1/l2 and masses m1 at elbow,m2 distal; torques τ1/τ2. Footer 7.
notes.1752: Phase 1 specifies an MLP with widths 6–30–20–2, sigmoid activation and backpropagation. Nominal synthetic data span beyond the physical operating region. The reported 1.5 million iterations and average error below 5% are experiment-specific, not a universal stop guarantee or permission to exceed real actuator limits. Printed footer 8 inspected separately.
notes.1753: Phase 2 uses bounded sinusoidal torques, frequencies below half the joint natural frequency and an example cap of 5 Hz. It reports 58,000 samples at 5 ms intervals, then 100 fine-tuning iterations. Validation uses novel torque inputs, ODE integration and real-motion comparison. The sample rate is 200 Hz; endpoint span is 289.995 s under consecutive sampling. Printed footer 9 inspected separately.
notes.1754: The2R inverse-dynamics example has l1=l2=1 m, m1=m2=1 kg as point masses at the link tips, and g=9.81 m/s². MLP regression takes joint positions, velocities and accelerations to two torques. The figure measures θ1 from horizontal and θ2 from the first-link extension. Its input box interleaves joint triples, unlike the later grouped code order. The learned predictor need not expose parameters at inference, but synthetic label generation uses known parameters. Footer10.
notes.1755: The printed mass matrix has M11=(m1+m2)l1²+m2l2²+2m1l1l2cosθ2, M12=M21=m2l2²+m2l1l2cosθ2, and M22=m2l2². The cross term in M11 prints m1, but the illustrated distal point-mass model requires m2. Equal example masses mask the discrepancy. The full geometry and all equations were read. Footer11.
notes.1756: The slide defines h=m2l1l2sinθ2, C1=−h θdot2²−2h θdot1θdot2 and C2=h θdot1². Gravity entries are g1=(m1+m2)g l1cosθ1+m2g l2cos(θ1+θ2) and g2=m2g l2cos(θ1+θ2). Both torque row expansions include inertia, velocity-product and gravity terms. Cosine gravity matches the horizontal angle reference. C is already a force vector, so it is not multiplied by velocity again. Footer12.
notes.1757: The ordered input is [q1,q2,q̇1,q̇2,q̈1,q̈2], with two torque targets. Angles span ±π, velocities ±2π and accelerations ±10. There are 50,000 independent random state tuples. Uniform joint coordinates do not imply uniform Cartesian endpoint density or a connected motion trajectory. Printed footer 13 inspected separately.
notes.1758: Every import and the complete vectorized inverse_dynamics function were inspected. Its M11 cross coefficient uses m2, unlike the m1 printed on page 1755. All C, gravity and row-expansion terms were checked. Unit masses and lengths and g=9.81 are explicit. Printed footer 14 inspected separately.
notes.1759: Six independent NumPy uniform draws have no displayed dataset seed. Column stacking gives X with 50,000 rows and six columns and Y with two columns. The 90:10 split has random_state=42, which does not retroactively seed data generation. Printed footer 15 inspected separately.
notes.1760: Pipeline contains StandardScaler and MLPRegressor with hidden widths 256,256,128, tanh, max_iter=500, learning_rate_init=0.001 and random_state=42. Training-only input statistics are used; targets are not scaled. max_iter is a maximum epoch count, not a guaranteed number of updates. Printed footer 16 inspected separately.
notes.1761: The code computes per-joint RMSE by averaging squared errors before taking the square root. Reported values are 0.6311 and 0.3734 N·m. The adjacent metric graphic lacks the mean operation. No positive-definite inertia structure is imposed on the plain torque MLP. Printed footer 17 inspected separately.
notes.1762: Both complete torque plots were inspected: true blue and predicted red dashed traces, shoulder above and elbow below, time from 0 to about 12.6 s. Small nonzero deviations are visible. The course notebook link was not retrieved; no closed-loop stability inference is supported by this plot alone. Printed footer 18 inspected separately.
notes.1763: H(q) is described as a symmetric positive-definite inertia matrix and V(q) as scalar potential. Configuration-only input applies to these subnetworks; the full Euler–Lagrange torque still needs velocity and acceleration. Printed footer 19 inspected separately.
notes.1764: The printed equation subtracts half the gradient of T, while T is defined as q̇ᵀHq̇ without one-half and labelled kinetic energy. This is consistent only if T is twice physical kinetic energy. Physical K=0.5q̇ᵀHq̇ requires subtraction of its full gradient. Printed footer 20 inspected separately.
notes.1765: All blue H and green V branches, derivative arrows and torque summation were inspected. Here T already includes one-half, but its gradient is halved again: a genuine normalization discrepancy. The position-only input drawing also omits the motion variables needed by the physical computation. Printed footer 21 inspected separately.
notes.1766: The same point-mass 2R model is learned with structured PyTorch rather than the black-box scikit-learn MLP. The reported 5,000 versus 50,000 samples illustrate possible data efficiency, not a universal tenfold guarantee. Printed footer 22 inspected separately.
notes.1767: Imports and the complete analytical torque generator were read. The M11 cross coefficient is m2. Adam is expanded as Adaptive Moment Estimation. The analytical label generator is separate from the learned H and V subnetworks. Printed footer 23 inspected separately.
notes.1768: The 5,000 samples produce Q,DQ,DDQ,TAU tensors, each with two float32 columns. Aligned slices give 4,500 training rows and 500 test rows. No NumPy or PyTorch seed is displayed. Printed footer 24 inspected separately.
notes.1769: The class call uses width 64 and two hidden layers; Adam has learning rate 0.001 and weight decay 0.0001. MSELoss, 500 epochs, batch size 128 and floor-divided 35 batches are printed. Each epoch uses 4,480 rows and drops 20 shuffled rows. zero_grad, backward and step ordering was checked. DeLaN2R itself is absent from the lecture. Printed footer 25 inspected separately.
notes.1770: The full logarithmic training-loss plot was read. It falls sharply at first and more slowly later, with visible upward fluctuations. This is training MSE, not test RMSE or a proof of generalization. Printed footer 26 inspected separately.
